text:
maya: Heads up — tiny canary deployment shows a regression when MoE routing is enabled with TP=2 / PP=2. Latency tail jumps and token throughput drops. nvprof timeline points to heavy NCCL alltoallv activity during token fanout.

maya: profiler snippet:
```
nvprof:  NCCL_alltoallv  58.2%  1.12ms  kernel  device 0
nvprof:  cudaMemcpyAsync 12.4%  0.24ms  copy  device 0->1
nvprof:  custom_router  6.5%   0.12ms  host
```

rick: Can you paste the GPU timeline / flamegraph? Is it all-to-all in forward or also in kv-sync?

maya: attaching a tiny timeline excerpt — the alltoall spikes align with route boundary (token boundary where routing fanout increases). Also seeing KV cache miss churn when tokens hop experts across ranks.

maya: mini timeline (simplified):
```
[0ms] compute chunk 1
[1ms] alltoallv (fanout 48->192)  <-- big spike
[3ms] compute chunk 2
[4ms] kv-fetch remote (cache miss)
[5ms] alltoallv reduce
```

nina: Are we sure kernel selection is choosing the vectorized/fused attention path for short sequences? If we fall back to generic kernels, extra device syncs can amplify alltoall cost. Try `kernel_policy: "prefer_fused_short_seq"`.

maya: Good call — current kernel selector picks `attn_generic` for seq=128 in some sharded paths. Changing policy reduces compute by ~8% but alltoall still dominates when fanout > 64.

tomas: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) increase microbatching (microbatch_size 1->4) to amortize alltoall; 2) enable comm/compute overlap: `overlap_comm_compute: true` + NCCL async streams. Did you try overlap?

maya: tried overlap. It helps when alltoalls are back-to-back, but stalls remain because routing is creating many small alltoalls with different partners each step — streams can't hide the latency when collectives change shape.

perf-bot: nightly-perf: moerouter-canary (17919xx) +12% latency vs baseline. Top stack: moerouter -> nccl_alltoallv -> kv_remote_fetch.

katie: Short-term mitigation: prune tiny routes that contribute <2% of tokens (route_prune_threshold: 0.02) — reduces number of small sends. Also consider `kv_shard_by_expert: true` so KV lives with expert compute and we avoid cross-rank reads.

rick: Could we compress routing indices before alltoall (run-length or delta encode) to reduce message sizes and collective scheduling overhead? Or combine small sends into one buffer per pair per step?

maya: We measured message-count vs message-size. The cost is more correlated with message count and partner churn than raw bytes. Combining buffers per-destination per-step helps. I'll sketch a patch that aggregates per-destination buffers and posts fewer alltoallv calls.

maya: quick repro command for anyone who wants to run locally:
```
./bench/run_moe.sh --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --microbatch 1 --profiling --nvprof --kernel-policy default
```

maya: Also observed KV cache thrash: routing variance across steps causes same token to be fetched from different expert ranks so cache hit-rate drops. Possible longer-term fix: sticky-routing (prefer same expert for short-token-history) or local KV replication for hot tokens.

tomas: For perf investigation: collect `heapmap` (per-rank message counts), `nvprof` timeline, and `router_hist` (per-token fanout distribution). If someone posts those I can try a replay-based micro-optimizer.

maya: I'll open a ticket with artifacts and heapmap. Creating REDWOOD-7891 and will upload logs + perf traces.

katie: Temporary config we pushed to a few canaries: `route_prune_threshold: 0.02`, `aggregate_to_pair_buffers: true`, `overlap_comm_compute: true`. Observed ~6% throughput improvement and 30% fewer small alltoall calls. Not a full fix but reduces the tail.

rick: Nice. Can you link the canary runs? Also add suggested kernel change to the perf-run checklist so we can A/B.

maya: Canary link: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/1792003 (profile + heapmap). Will attach patch diff to REDWOOD-7891 and request review from eng-runtime.

maya: TL;DR — root cause: routing-induced partner churn + many small alltoalls + KV cache misses. Short-term: prune tiny routes + aggregate per-destination buffers + overlap. Medium-term: sticky-routing / kv colocation + smarter kernel selection for sharded paths. Volunteers to triage today? :eyes:
